source_text: Sub eadem Abrahae mentione, dum ipso sensu reuincatur. adhuc, inquit, secundum hominem dico: dum essemus paruuli, sub elementis mundi eramus positi ad deseruiendum eis. atquin non est hoc humanitus dictum, non enim exemplum est, sed ueritas. quis enim paruulus — utique sensu, quod sunt nationes — non elementis subiectus est mundi, quae pro deo suspicit? illud autem fuit, quod tum secundum hominem dixit: sed tamen testamentum hominis nemo spernit aut superordinat. exemplo enim humani testamenti permanentis diuinum tuebatur: Abrahae dictae sunt promissiones et semini eius. non dixit 'seminibus*, quasi pluribus, sed 'semini' tamquam uni, quod est Christus. erubescat spongia Marcionis! nisi quod ex abundanti retracto quae abstulit, cum ualidius sit illum ex his reuinci, quae seruauit. cum autem euenit impleri tempus, misit deus filium suum, utique is, qui etiam ipsorum temporum deus est, quibus saeculum constat, qui signa quoque temporum ordinauit, soles et lunas et sidera et stellas, qui filii denique sui reuelationem in extremitatem temporum et disposuit et praedicauit: in nouissimis diebus erit manifestus mons domini, et: in nouissimis diebus effundam de meo spiritu in omnem carnem, secundum Iohelem. ipsius erat sustinuisse tempus impleri, cuius erat etiam finis temporis sicut initium.
pass_a_gloss: Under the same mention of Abraham, while he is being convinced by the same sense, he says, still, I speak according to man: while we were children, we were placed under the elements of the world to serve them. But this is not said in a human way, for it is not an example, but truth. For which child - certainly in sense, because they are nations - is not subject to the elements of the world, which it regards as God? That, however, was what he said according to man: but nevertheless, no one despises or superordinates a human testament. For by the example of a human testament, he was defending the divine one: promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. He did not say 'seeds', as if many, but 'seed', just as one, which is Christ. Let Marcion's sponge be ashamed! Unless, indeed, I retract from abundance what I have taken away, since it is more valid to convict him from those things which he has preserved. When, however, the time came to be fulfilled, God sent his Son, certainly he who is also the God of those times, by which the age consists, who also arranged the signs of the times, suns and moons and stars and constellations, who finally disposed and predicted the revelation of his Son at the end of times: in the last days, the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, and: in the last days, I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh, according to Joel 2:28, and also according to other scriptures, in the last days, the mountain of the Lord will be established, as it is written in Micah 4:1. It was his to sustain the time to be fulfilled, whose was also the end of time, just as the beginning.

pass_b_english: When talking about Abraham, the argument is won with the same logic. The point is, when we were like children, we were under the control of the world's basic elements, forced to serve them. But let's be clear: this isn't just some human analogy - it's the truth. Every nation, in a sense, is like a child, subject to the world's elements, which they often mistake for God. The fact that no one disregards or overrides a human will is what Paul uses to defend God's covenant. He's saying that just as a human will is binding, God's promises to Abraham and his descendant are also set in stone. Note that it says 'descendant', not 'descendants' - a clear reference to Christ. Marcion should be embarrassed by his attempts to distort this. Unless, of course, I'm taking back what I previously argued against, since it's actually more effective to challenge him using the parts of scripture he accepts. When the time was right, God sent His Son, who is not only the Son of God but also the Lord of time itself, governing the ages, orchestrating the movements of the sun, moon, stars, and constellations. He predetermined and prophesied the revelation of His Son for the end times, as stated in Joel 2:28, where it says, 'I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh in the last days.' Similarly, Micah 4:1 says, 'In the last days, the mountain of the Lord will be established.' It was God's prerogative to oversee the fulfillment of time, just as He controls both the beginning and the end of time (Joel 2:28, Micah 4:1).

review.notes: Pass B introduces significant agency and content not present in the Locked Latin. 1. It attributes the defense of the covenant to 'Paul' ('what Paul uses to defend God's covenant'), whereas the Latin says 'exemplo enim humani testamenti permanentis diuinum tuebatur' (for by the example of a human testament, he was defending the divine one), referring to the speaker/author or the logic of the argument, not Paul. 2. It adds 'not only the Son of God but also the Lord of time itself', which is a theological expansion not found in 'qui etiam ipsorum temporum deus est'. 3. It adds 'He predetermined and prophesied' where the Latin says 'qui... disposuit et praedicauit' (who... disposed and predicted). 4. Pass B adds 'He controls both the beginning and the end of time', whereas the Latin says 'cuius erat etiam finis temporis sicut initium' (whose was also the end of time, just as the beginning).
reasons: Pass B introduces 'what Paul uses to defend God's covenant', but the Latin 'exemplo enim humani testamenti permanentis diuinum tuebatur' does not mention Paul.
Pass B adds 'not only the Son of God but also the Lord of time itself', which is not in the Latin 'qui etiam ipsorum temporum deus est'.
Pass B adds 'He controls both the beginning and the end of time', which is an expansion of 'cuius erat etiam finis temporis sicut initium'.

review.notes: source: 'in nouissimis diebus erit manifestus mons domini', English: 'in the last days, the mountain of the Lord will be manifest'; source: 'in nouissimis diebus effundam de meo spiritu in omnem carnem', English: 'in the last days, I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh'; source: 'in nouissimis diebus erit manifestus mons domini', English: 'in the last days, the mountain of the Lord will be established'
reasons: The translation fails to preserve the exact wording of the scriptural citations. For example, 'in nouissimis diebus erit manifestus mons domini' is translated as 'in the last days, the mountain of the Lord will be manifest' in the source, but in the English translation, it is rendered as 'in the last days, the mountain of the Lord will be established,' which is a paraphrase of Micah 4:1 rather than a direct match. Similarly, 'in nouissimis diebus effundam de meo spiritu in omnem carnem' is translated as 'in the last days, I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh,' which is a correct rendering of Joel 2:28, but the English translation also includes 'as it is written in Micah 4:1,' which is not in the source text. The source does not mention Micah 4:1 in the context of 'in the last days, the mountain of the Lord will be established,' and the English translation adds this reference without justification. Additionally, the source text does not include the phrase 'Joel 2:28, Micah 4:1' in the passage, but the English translation includes it, which is an addition not present in the source.
